analysis: The closest option combines a multi-course quantitative foundation with economic modelling and regression. Calculus, linear algebra, probability, numerical methods and linear systems provide mathematical depth. Introductory economics, microeconomics, macroeconomics and public economics address economic theory and policy. Econometrics adds estimation and inference, and machine learning adds a complementary predictive approach. Replacing reinforcement learning and AI ethics with public economics and advanced calculus increases weight on quantitative economics.

The second option gives greater weight to software design, computer vision, probabilistic decision models, optimisation, reinforcement learning and AI ethics. Neural networks follow machine learning. Programming precedes the fixed early slot for optimisation, with mathematics developed alongside it. AI in business connects methods to organisational consequences without replacing technical depth.

The third option uses accounting and corporate finance, banking and financial markets, and international macroeconomics as substantive applications for statistics and econometrics. Consumer engagement, empirical market research, digital strategy and organisational psychology add distinct decisions about markets and organisations. The finance courses do not teach actuarial risk or insurance reserving.

Pairwise differences are 45, 52.5 and 60 EC each way. Five offering conflicts were resolved through course reassessment and scheduling. The current plan makes meaningful partial alignments without collapsing the separate probability, statistical theory, econometrics, time-series or insurance components. The two thesis seminar courses share one research trajectory and the optional UCR element sits beside the research project only.
constructionStop: Three coherent, distinct options reach the programme limit.
